If `None`, defaults to 30 minutes.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `std::process::Command` - Configured command ready for execution via `spawn()` or `status()`.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::util::build_cargo_test_command;\n/// use std::process::Command;\n///\n/// // With default 30-minute timeout\n/// let cmd = build_cargo_test_command(None);\n///\n/// // With custom 45-minute timeout\n/// let cmd = build_cargo_test_command(Some(45));\n///\n/// // Execute the command\n/// let status = cmd.status().expect(\"failed to execute cargo test\");\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Timeout Behavior\n///\n/// - The `timeout` command will send `SIGTERM` to the cargo process when the timeout is reached.\n/// - If the process does not exit within 1 second after `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL` is sent.\n/// - Exit code 124 indicates the timeout was triggered (see `timeout(1)` man page).\n///\n/// # Default Value\n///\n/// When `timeout_minutes` is `None`, the default is **30 minutes**.\npub fn build_cargo_test_command(timeout_minutes: Option<u64>) -> std::process::Command {\n    let timeout_seconds = timeout_minutes.unwrap_or(30) * 60;\n\n    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(\"timeout\");\n    cmd.arg(format!(\"{}\", timeout_seconds))\n        .arg(\"cargo\")\n        .arg(\"test\")\n        .arg(\"--all-targets\")\n        .arg(\"--\")\n        .arg(\"--nocapture\");\n\n    cmd\n}\n\n/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n///\n/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n///\n/// This function handles all errors internally and never panics. If system\n/// time is unavailable or chrono formatting fails (e.g., due to extreme\n/// system clock values that overflow chrono's internal calculations), it\n/// falls back to the Unix epoch timestamp (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and\n/// logs an error message to stderr.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `String` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or the epoch\n///   timestamp as a fallback if time capture fails\n///\n/// # Fallback Behavior\n///\n/// When the system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n/// or chrono formatting fails, this function:\n/// - Returns `\"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\"` (Unix epoch)\n/// - Logs an error message to stderr with failure details\n/// - Never panics, ensuring the function is safe to call in production\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp;\n///\n/// let now = capture_timestamp();\n/// println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", now);\n/// // Output: \"2026-08-13T14:30:00Z\" (or epoch on failure)\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Performance\n///\n/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n///\n/// # Error Handling\n///\n/// For use cases that need to distinguish between success and failure,\n/// use [`capture_timestamp_result()`] instead, which returns a `Result`.\npub fn capture_timestamp() -> String {\n    capture_timestamp_result().unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n        eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}. Using epoch fallback.\", e);\n        // Unix epoch as ISO 8601 timestamp (fallback when system time fails)\n        \"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\".to_string()\n    })\n}\n\n/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n///\n/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n///\n/// This is the fallible version of [`capture_timestamp()`] that returns\n/// a `Result` instead of handling errors internally. Use this when you\n/// need to distinguish between successful timestamp capture and failures.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Result<String>` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or an\n///   error if time capture fails\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// This function returns an error if:\n/// - The system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n/// - Chrono formatting fails to produce an ISO 8601 string (e.g., due to\n///   extreme system clock values)\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp_result;\n///\n/// match capture_timestamp_result() {\n///     Ok(timestamp) => println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", timestamp),\n///     Err(e) => eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}\", e),\n/// }\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Performance\n///\n/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\npub fn capture_timestamp_result() -> Result<String> {\n    // Use catch_unwind to handle any potential panics from chrono operations\n    // This protects against extreme edge cases like system clock overflow\n    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n        let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n        now.to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)\n    }));\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(timestamp) => Ok(timestamp),\n        Err(_) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\"\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse the backend name from a binary's version output.\n///\n/// Runs the specified binary with the given version command arguments,\n/// captures stdout, and extracts the backend name (first word of output).\n///\n/// This function includes ETXTBSY (errno 26) retry logic to handle the race\n/// condition where a binary written to disk immediately before execution\n/// transiently reports \"Text file busy\".\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `binary_path` - Path to the binary to execute\n/// * `version_args` - Arguments to pass for version check (e.g., `[\"--version\"]`)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Result<String>` - The extracted backend name, or an error if:\n///   - Binary not found\n///   - Binary exits with non-zero code\n///   - Output is empty or unparseable\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::util::parse_backend_name_from_version;\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n/// let backend = parse_backend_name_from_version(\n///     Path::new(\"/usr/local/bin/bf\"),\n///     &[\"--version\"]\n/// )?;\n/// assert_eq!(backend, \"bf\");\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub fn parse_backend_name_from_version(\n    binary_path: &std::path::Path,\n    version_args: &[&str],\n) -> Result<String> {\n    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n    use std::thread;\n\n    // Check if binary exists\n    if !binary_path.exists() {\n        anyhow::bail!(\"binary not found at {}\", binary_path.display());\n    }\n\n    // ETXTBSY retry logic: retry with backoff when the kernel reports \"Text file busy\"\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    let max_attempts = 5;\n    let backoff_ms = 20;\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        let result = Command::new(binary_path)\n            .args(version_args)\n            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n            .output();\n\n        match result {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                // Check exit status\n                if !output.status.success() {\n                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n                    anyhow::bail!(\n                        \"binary {} exited with code {}: {}\",\n                        binary_path.display(),\n                        output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\n                        stderr.trim()\n                    );\n                }\n\n                // Capture stdout\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\n\n                // Extract backend name (first word)\n                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\n                    anyhow::anyhow!(\n                        \"binary {} produced empty or unparseable version output\",\n                        binary_path.display()\n                    )\n                })?;\n\n                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\",\n                        binary_path.display(),\n                        version_args\n                    )\n                })\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // All retries exhausted\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\")).with_context(\n        || {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\",\n                binary_path.display(),\n                max_attempts\n            )\n        },\n    )\n}\n\n/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n///\n/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n///\n/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n#[cfg(test)]\npub(crate) mod test_env {\n    use std::ffi::OsString;\n    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n\n    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n\n    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\n    ///\n    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\n    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\n    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\n    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\n    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\n    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\n    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\n        \"HOME\",\n        \"PATH\",\n        \"NEEDLE_HOME\",\n        \"NEEDLE_EVENTS\",\n        \"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\",\n    ];\n\n    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\n    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\n    }\n\n    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n        fn drop(&mut self) {\n            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\n                restore(key, value);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n        match value {\n            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n    ///\n    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n    /// private instead.\n    ///\n    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n\n        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n\n        let root =\n            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n        let dir = root\n            .path()\n            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n        dir\n    }\n\n    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n    ///\n    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n        let guard = EnvGuard {\n            saved: GUARDED_VARS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|&key| (key, std::env::var_os(key)))\n                .collect(),\n        };\n        (lock, guard)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use chrono::{Datelike, error if time capture fails\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// This function returns an error if:\n/// - The system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n/// - Chrono formatting fails to produce an ISO 8601 string (e.g., due to\n///   extreme system clock values)\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp_result;\n///\n/// match capture_timestamp_result() {\n///     Ok(timestamp) => println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", timestamp),\n///     Err(e) => eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}\", e),\n/// }\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Performance\n///\n/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\npub fn capture_timestamp_result() -> Result<String> {\n    // Use catch_unwind to handle any potential panics from chrono operations\n    // This protects against extreme edge cases like system clock overflow\n    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n        let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n        now.to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)\n    }));\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(timestamp) => Ok(timestamp),\n        Err(_) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\"\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse the backend name from a binary's version output.\n///\n/// Runs the specified binary with the given version command arguments,\n/// captures stdout, and extracts the backend name (first word of output).\n///\n/// This function includes ETXTBSY (errno 26) retry logic to handle the race\n/// condition where a binary written to disk immediately before execution\n/// transiently reports \"Text file busy\".\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `binary_path` - Path to the binary to execute\n/// * `version_args` - Arguments to pass for version check (e.g., `[\"--version\"]`)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Result<String>` - The extracted backend name, or an error if:\n///   - Binary not found\n///   - Binary exits with non-zero code\n///   - Output is empty or unparseable\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::util::parse_backend_name_from_version;\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n/// let backend = parse_backend_name_from_version(\n///     Path::new(\"/usr/local/bin/bf\"),\n///     &[\"--version\"]\n/// )?;\n/// assert_eq!(backend, \"bf\");\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub fn parse_backend_name_from_version(\n    binary_path: &std::path::Path,\n    version_args: &[&str],\n) -> Result<String> {\n    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n    use std::thread;\n\n    // Check if binary exists\n    if !binary_path.exists() {\n        anyhow::bail!(\"binary not found at {}\", binary_path.display());\n    }\n\n    // ETXTBSY retry logic: retry with backoff when the kernel reports \"Text file busy\"\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    let max_attempts = 5;\n    let backoff_ms = 20;\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        let result = Command::new(binary_path)\n            .args(version_args)\n            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n            .output();\n\n        match result {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                // Check exit status\n                if !output.status.success() {\n                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n                    anyhow::bail!(\n                        \"binary {} exited with code {}: {}\",\n                        binary_path.display(),\n                        output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\n                        stderr.trim()\n                    );\n                }\n\n                // Capture stdout\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\n\n                // Extract backend name (first word)\n                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\n                    anyhow::anyhow!(\n                        \"binary {} produced empty or unparseable version output\",\n                        binary_path.display()\n                    )\n                })?;\n\n                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\",\n                        binary_path.display(),\n                        version_args\n                    )\n                })\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // All retries exhausted\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\")).with_context(\n        || {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\",\n                binary_path.display(),\n                max_attempts\n            )\n        },\n    )\n}\n\n/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n///\n/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n///\n/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n#[cfg(test)]\npub(crate) mod test_env {\n    use std::ffi::OsString;\n    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n\n    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n\n    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\n    ///\n    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\n    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\n    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\n    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\n    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\n    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\n    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\n        \"HOME\",\n        \"PATH\",\n        \"NEEDLE_HOME\",\n        \"NEEDLE_EVENTS\",\n        \"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\",\n    ];\n\n    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\n    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\n    }\n\n    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n        fn drop(&mut self) {\n            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\n                restore(key, value);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n        match value {\n            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n    ///\n    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n    /// private instead.\n    ///\n    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n\n        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n\n        let root =\n            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n        let dir = root\n            .path()\n            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n        dir\n    }\n\n    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n    ///\n    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n        let guard = EnvGuard {\n            saved: GUARDED_VARS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|&key| (key, std::env::var_os(key)))\n                .collect(),\n        };\n        (lock, guard)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use chrono::{Datelike, parse_backend_name_from_version(\n///     Path::new(\"/usr/local/bin/bf\"),\n///     &[\"--version\"]\n/// )?;\n/// assert_eq!(backend, \"bf\");\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub fn parse_backend_name_from_version(\n    binary_path: &std::path::Path,\n    version_args: &[&str],\n) -> Result<String> {\n    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n    use std::thread;\n\n    // Check if binary exists\n    if !binary_path.exists() {\n        anyhow::bail!(\"binary not found at {}\", binary_path.display());\n    }\n\n    // ETXTBSY retry logic: retry with backoff when the kernel reports \"Text file busy\"\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    let max_attempts = 5;\n    let backoff_ms = 20;\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        let result = Command::new(binary_path)\n            .args(version_args)\n            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n            .output();\n\n        match result {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        binary = %binary_path.display(),\n                        function = \"parse_backend_name_from_version\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n\n                // Check exit status\n                if !output.status.success() {\n                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n                    anyhow::bail!(\n                        \"binary {} exited with code {}: {}\",\n                        binary_path.display(),\n                        output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\n                        stderr.trim()\n                    );\n                }\n\n                // Capture stdout\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\n\n                // Extract backend name (first word)\n                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\n                    anyhow::anyhow!(\n                        \"binary {} produced empty or unparseable version output\",\n                        binary_path.display()\n                    )\n                })?;\n\n                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\",\n                        binary_path.display(),\n                        version_args\n                    )\n                })\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // All retries exhausted\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\")).with_context(\n        || {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\",\n                binary_path.display(),\n                max_attempts\n            )\n        },\n    )\n}\n\n/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n///\n/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n///\n/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n#[cfg(test)]\npub(crate) mod test_env {\n    use std::ffi::OsString;\n    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n\n    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n\n    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\n    ///\n    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\n    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\n    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\n    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\n    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\n    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\n    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\n        \"HOME\",\n        \"PATH\",\n        \"NEEDLE_HOME\",\n        \"NEEDLE_EVENTS\",\n        \"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\",\n    ];\n\n    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\n    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\n    }\n\n    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n        fn drop(&mut self) {\n            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\n                restore(key, value);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n        match value {\n            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n    ///\n    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n    /// private instead.\n    ///\n    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n\n        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n\n        let root =\n            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n        let dir = root\n            .path()\n            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n        dir\n    }\n\n    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n    ///\n    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n        let guard = EnvGuard {\n            saved: GUARDED_VARS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|&key| (key, std::env::var_os(key)))\n                .collect(),\n        };\n        (lock, guard)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};\n    use std::env;\n    use std::path::PathBuf;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_is_tilde_prefix_with_tilde_slash() {\n        // \"~/foo\" should return true (tilde prefix)\n extract_tokens(extraction: &TokenExtraction, stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> TokenUsage {\n    match extraction {\n        TokenExtraction::None => TokenUsage::default(),\n        TokenExtraction::JsonField {\n            input_path,\n            output_path,\n        } => extract_tokens_json(stdout, input_path, output_path),\n        TokenExtraction::Regex {\n            pattern,\n            input_group,\n            output_group,\n        } => {\n            // Search both stdout and stderr for the pattern.\n            let combined = format!(\"{stdout}\\n{stderr}\");\n            extract_tokens_regex(&combined, pattern, *input_group, *output_group)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract tokens from JSON output using dot-separated path notation.\nfn extract_tokens_json(stdout: &str, input_path: &str, output_path: &str) -> TokenUsage {\n    let parsed: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(stdout) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(_) => return TokenUsage::default(),\n    };\n\n    let input_tokens = resolve_json_path(&parsed, input_path).and_then(|v| v.as_u64());\n    let output_tokens = resolve_json_path(&parsed, output_path).and_then(|v| v.as_u64());\n\n    TokenUsage {\n        input_tokens,\n        output_tokens,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Resolve a dot-separated path in a JSON value (e.g., `result.usage.input_tokens`).\nfn resolve_json_path<'a>(\n    value: &'a serde_json::Value,\n    path: &str,\n) -> Option<&'a serde_json::Value> {\n    let mut current = value;\n    for key in path.split('.') {\n        current = current.get(key)?;\n    }\n    Some(current)\n}\n\n/// Extract tokens from text using a regex with numbered capture groups.\nfn extract_tokens_regex(\n    text: &str,\n    pattern: &str,\n    input_group: usize,\n    output_group: usize,\n) -> TokenUsage {\n    let re = match Regex::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(r) => r,\n        Err(_) => return TokenUsage::default(),\n    };\n\n    let caps = match re.captures(text) {\n        Some(c) => c,\n        None => return TokenUsage::default(),\n    };\n\n    let parse_group = |group: usize| -> Option<u64> {\n        caps.get(group)?\n            .as_str()\n            .replace(',', \"\")\n            .parse::<u64>()\n            .ok()\n    };\n\n    TokenUsage {\n        input_tokens: parse_group(input_group),\n        output_tokens: parse_group(output_group),\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// TimeoutPolicy\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Which timeout configuration mode is active for an adapter.\n///\n/// An adapter can use:\n/// - Legacy single timeout (`timeout_secs`)\n/// - New two-field timeout (`idle_timeout_secs` + `hard_timeout_secs`)\n/// - Global config fallback (no adapter-specific timeout set)\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TimeoutPolicy {\n    /// Legacy single timeout mode (`timeout_secs` is set).\n    Legacy,\n    /// New two-field timeout mode (at least one of `idle_timeout_secs` or `hard_timeout_secs` is set).\n    New {\n        /// Whether idle timeout is configured (non-zero).\n        idle_enabled: bool,\n        /// Whether hard timeout is configured (non-zero).\n        hard_enabled: bool,\n    },\n    /// No adapter-specific timeout; uses global config default.\n    Global,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentAdapter\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Configuration for a single agent adapter, loaded from YAML or embedded.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct AgentAdapter {\n    /// Unique adapter name (e.g., `claude-sonnet`).\n    pub name: String,\n    /// Human-readable description.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub description: Option<String>,\n    /// Agent CLI binary name (for documentation / version checks).\n    pub agent_cli: String,\n    /// Command to check the agent version.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub version_command: Option<String>,\n    /// How the prompt is delivered to the agent.\n    #[serde(default = \"default_input_method\")]\n    pub input_method: InputMethod,\n    /// Shell command template with variable placeholders.\n    ///\n    /// Supported variables: `{workspace}`, `{prompt_file}`, `{bead_id}`, `{model}`.\n    pub invoke_template: String,\n    /// Extra environment variables set for the agent process.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub environment: HashMap<String, String>,\n    /// Timeout in seconds (0 = use global config timeout).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Idle timeout in seconds (0 = no idle deadline).\n    ///\n    /// When implemented, will kill the agent if no stdout/stderr activity\n    /// is detected for this duration. This is a data-model-only field;\n    /// validation and enforcement logic will be added in a follow-up.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub idle_timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Hard timeout in seconds (0 = no hard deadline).\n    ///\n    /// When implemented, will enforce an absolute maximum execution time\n    /// regardless of agent activity. This is a data-model-only field;\n    /// enforcement logic will be added in a follow-up.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub hard_timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// AI provider name (informational).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n    /// Model identifier (substituted as `{model}` in the template).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// How to extract token usage from agent output.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub token_extraction: TokenExtraction,\n    /// Optional binary/script to normalize agent stdout into universal JSONL.\n    ///\n    /// When set, the named binary is invoked with the raw agent stdout piped to\n    /// its stdin.  Its stdout replaces the raw output for all downstream\n    /// processing (token extraction, outcome parsing, …).\n    ///\n    /// Example adapter YAML:\n    /// ```yaml\n    /// output_transform: \"needle-transform-claude\"\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// The binary must be present on PATH; `needle test-agent <name>` will\n    /// report an error if it cannot be found.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub output_transform: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness name for velocity-aware claim scoring.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub harness: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness version for velocity-aware claim scoring.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub harness_version: Option<String>,\n}\n\nfn default_input_method() -> InputMethod {\n    InputMethod::Stdin\n}\n\nimpl AgentAdapter {\n    /// Effective timeout as a `Duration`, falling back to the global config.\n    pub fn effective_timeout(&self, global_timeout_secs: u64) -> Duration {\n        let secs = if self.timeout_secs > 0 {\n            self.timeout_secs\n        } else {\n            global_timeout_secs\n        };\n        if secs == 0 {\n            Duration::ZERO\n        } else {\n            Duration::from_secs(secs)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the GenAI system name for this adapter.\n    ///\n    /// Follows OTel semantic conventions for `gen_ai.system`, which identifies\n    /// the AI system/platform (e.g., \"anthropic\", \"openai\", \"local\").\n    /// Defaults to \"local\" if no provider is configured.\n    pub fn gen_ai_system(&self) -> &str {\n        self.provider.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"local\")\n    }\n\n    /// Active timeout policy for this adapter.\n    ///\n    /// Distinguishes between legacy single timeout and the new two-field\n    /// (idle + hard) timeout model.\n    pub fn timeout_policy(&self) -> TimeoutPolicy {\n        let has_legacy = self.timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_idle = self.idle_timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_hard = self.hard_timeout_secs > 0;\n\n        if has_legacy {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Legacy\n        } else if has_idle || has_hard {\n            TimeoutPolicy::New {\n                idle_enabled: has_idle,\n                hard_enabled: has_hard,\n            }\n        } else {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Global\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Human-readable description of the active timeout policy.\n    ///\n    /// Shows which timeout mode is active and the configured values.\n    pub fn timeout_description(&self, global_timeout_secs: u64) -> String {\n        match self.timeout_policy() {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Legacy => {\n                format!(\"legacy: {}s (single timeout)\", self.timeout_secs)\n            }\n            TimeoutPolicy::New {\n                idle_enabled,\n                hard_enabled,\n            } => {\n                let mut parts = Vec::new();\n                parts.push(\"new:\".to_string());\n                if idle_enabled {\n                    parts.push(format!(\"idle={}s\", self.idle_timeout_secs));\n                }\n                if hard_enabled {\n                    parts.push(format!(\"hard={}s\", self.hard_timeout_secs));\n                }\n                if !idle_enabled && !hard_enabled {\n                    parts.push(\"both disabled\".to_string());\n                }\n                parts.join(\" \")\n            }\n            TimeoutPolicy::Global => {\n                if global_timeout_secs > 0 {\n                    format!(\"global: {}s (from config)\", global_timeout_secs)\n                } else {\n                    \"global: unlimited (0 = no timeout)\".to_string()\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity.\n    ///\n    /// Legacy `timeout_secs` and new `idle_timeout_secs`/`hard_timeout_secs`\n    /// cannot both be set. This preserves backward compatibility while allowing\n    /// the new two-field timeout model.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - `timeout_secs` is non-zero AND either `idle_timeout_secs` or `hard_timeout_secs` is non-zero\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// // Valid: legacy timeout alone\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_timeout_secs_only().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Valid: new timeout fields together\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_new_timeouts().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Valid: new timeout field alone (other set to 0)\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_idle_only().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Invalid: mixing legacy and new\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_mixed_timeouts().validate_timeouts().is_err());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn validate_timeouts(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let has_legacy = self.timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_idle = self.idle_timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_hard = self.hard_timeout_secs > 0;\n\n        if has_legacy && (has_idle || has_hard) {\n            bail!(\n                \"adapter '{}' has incompatible timeout configuration: \\\n                 legacy field 'timeout_secs' ({}) cannot be used together with new fields \\\n                 'idle_timeout_secs' ({}) or 'hard_timeout_secs' ({}). \\\n                 Use either timeout_secs alone (legacy) or idle_timeout_secs + hard_timeout_secs (new).\",\n                self.name,\n                self.timeout_secs,\n                self.idle_timeout_secs,\n                self.hard_timeout_secs\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Built-in adapters\n// Some(\"needle\".to_string()),\n        harness_version: Some(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Claude Code (Opus) built-in adapter.\nfn builtin_claude_opus() -> AgentAdapter
